body:
## Where this came from

The fuzzy gate only catches entries a tool already **flagged**. A confidently-wrong
translation nobody doubted passes every gate silently — `Compact` and `Dense` both
rendering as "Compact" in Dutch (`F-4079f1`) has no fuzzy flag at all.

The proposed tell needs no flag and no knowledge of the language: **two different
msgids rendering as the same string**. It found the real bugs in the fuzzy sweep
(`One column`/`Two columns` both meaning "Invalid read column"; `Black` meaning
"Back").

## Measured before proposing it as a gate, and it should NOT be one

Swept all **864** SPA-anchored msgids across every locale: **222** non-case-variant
clashes. The overwhelming majority are correct:

- **Languages without plural inflection.** `Author`/`Authors` → 作者, `Task`/`Tasks`
  → タスク, `{count} file rejected`/`{count} files rejected` → one Hungarian form.
  Nothing is wrong; the distinction does not exist in the target language.
- **English synonyms that legitimately share a translation.** `Mark as read` /
  `Mark read`; `Create account` / `Create an account`; `Could not create the shelf.` /
  `Could not create shelf.` These are our duplicates, not the translator's.

A gate on this would be 222 rows of noise, which is how a gate stops being read —
the same failure the follow-up board had when its largest section was our own
findings. **Keep it as a sweep, run it when anchoring new msgids, and read the
output.**

## The shortlist worth a human eye

Cases where the two msgids genuinely mean different things:

| locale | one output | serves | why it looks wrong |
|---|---|---|---|
| `es` | `Subir` | `Move up`, `Upload` | reorder vs. send a file — unrelated actions |
| `ru` | `Загрузка…` | `Uploading…`, `Loading…` | sending vs. waiting |
| `hu` | `Címkék` | `Tags`, `Categories` | distinct taxonomies in Calibre |
| `vi` | `Tìm kiếm` | `Search`, `Browse` | a query vs. an unfiltered list |
| `ja` | `既読` | `Yes`, `Read` | "yes" reading as "already read" |
| `zh_Hant_TW` | `上傳書籍` | `Upload books`, `Upload` | the generic action reads as book-specific |

Not fixed here: each needs someone who reads the language to confirm intent, and
guessing is what produced the fuzzy entries in the first place. Filed so the list
exists rather than being rediscovered.

## The reusable part

The two i18n failure classes need different instruments, and neither catches the
other:

- **flagged-and-wrong** → the fuzzy gate; blanket-clearing it ships nonsense
  (see `never-blanket-clear-fuzzy-po-entries` in project memory);
- **unflagged-and-wrong** → this sweep; it cannot be automated into a pass/fail
  because a shared translation is usually correct.
title: Two SPA msgids sharing one translation: a good diagnostic, a bad gate — 222 hits, a handful real
